avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce rabeprazole effectiveness
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; select alternative herbal supplement

caution_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Reduced gastric acid decreases calcium absorption; take 2+ hours apart
caution_supplements.action: Separate dosing by at least 2 hours; monitor for hypocalcemia with chronic use

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin B12
caution_supplements.mechanism: Long-term PPI use reduces intrinsic factor and B12 absorption
caution_supplements.action: Monitor B12 levels annually; consider supplementation if deficiency develops

caution_supplements.name: Iron supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Reduced gastric acid impairs non-heme iron absorption
caution_supplements.action: Take iron supplement 2+ hours before rabeprazole; monitor for anemia

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Decreased gastric acid reduces magnesium bioavailability
caution_supplements.action: Monitor magnesium levels with chronic PPI use; supplement if needed

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase rabeprazole levels
caution_foods.action: Limit grapefruit juice consumption; monitor for adverse effects

monitoring_notes: Monitor for vitamin B12, calcium, magnesium, and iron deficiencies with long-term use. Rabeprazole effectiveness may be compromised by CYP3A4 inducers; no food interactions significantly impair absorption.
